source: Rauhut & Pol 2019, Scientific Reports 9, Fig. 4a: time-calibrated reduced consensus of tetanurans placing Asfaltovenator; rectangular staircase, root left, tips right with thick range bars, grey stage bands, clade names beside the backbone, coloured boxes behind seven clades with their names. Panels b (homoplasy histogram) and c (a schematic tree) and the shared timescale strip are excluded. Image: census figure (1650x1792 px).
region_note: panel a (the tree, with its shaded time bands); b is a homoplasy histogram and the timescale strip below is shared, so it is left out; c is a schematic
attribution: Rauhut, O. W. M.; Pol, D. (2019). Probable basal allosauroid from the early Middle Jurassic Cañadón Asfalto Formation of Argentina highlights phylogenetic uncertainty in tetanuran theropod dinosaurs. Scientific Reports 9. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-019-53672-7. Fig. 4a. CC BY 4.0.
names_note: the paper's matrix taxa (census list, 68; the reduced consensus shows 57). Tips take the list spelling, which quotes four of them: "Coelophysis bauri", "S zigongensis" (printed S. zigongensis), "Yangchuano hepingensis" (printed Yangchuanosaurus hepingensis), "Sinraptor dongi"
gold_note: Tetanuran time tree (reduced consensus). The backbone is a staircase whose stems enter each vertical at its lower end. Internal labels: backbone names (Averostra, Tetanurae, Carnosauria, Allosauroidea), each matched to the vertical it is centred on, and the seven boxes (Ceratosauria, Coelurosauria, Spinosauridae, Megalosauridae, Piatnitzkysauridae, Metriacanthosauridae, Carcharodontosauria). Read by eye at 3-7x. 57 tips, 5 polytomies (3, 3, 3, 4, 4 children); 11 printed clade names kept as internal node labels. Random-sample case (seed 20261114). Topology transcribed from the figure image and checked node by node; topology only.
